title: Applying Epidemiological Herd Immunity Concepts to AI Model Portfolio Design

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a formal diversity threshold would give deployers and regulators a quantitative target. The epidemiological analogy provides a compelling and well-understood framework for policy communication.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires mathematical formalization of epidemiological models adapted to adversarial AI contexts. Heavy theoretical work involving probability theory and network modeling. Beyond beginner CS level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: formalize the threshold, compute it for current model distributions. The mathematical derivation plus empirical computation is a well-defined project.

novelty.reasoning: Web search found no existing work that formally applies epidemiological herd immunity models to AI model portfolio diversity. While AI monoculture risks are discussed conceptually and herd immunity modeling in networks is active (PNAS 2025), the specific cross-domain application — deriving a formal diversity threshold for AI model portfolios analogous to herd immunity thresholds — does not appear in the literature. The epidemiological analogy has been used loosely in cybersecurity (software diversity) but not formalized for AI model portfolios with adversarial robustness considerations. This is a genuinely novel cross-domain contribution.
